meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'along; by; about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm here about the job.
We're talking on the phone.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'which, who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Чтобы он вернул деньги, которые украл.
examples.trans: For him to give back the money he stole.

examples.text: Который ему город подарил! И откуда у Аллы Евгеньевны новая шуба!
examples.trans: Which the city donated to him! And where Alla Yevgenyevna got a new fur coat!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: А ты иди на биржу труда. Там есть работа.
examples.trans: You go to the job centre. There's work there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone, somebody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Ты что, не понимаешь? Я задавить кого-то мог!
examples.trans: Don't you understand? I could have run someone over!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there, thither', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю! Хочешь, сейчас и тебя туда увезут?
examples.trans: I know! Do you want them to take you there too right now?
They put bad meat in there for you.
Let's go there together.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
He's at our place.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('every, each').

examples.trans: Every day.
Every person.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my own', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'path, way, journey' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here is a movie: A Thorny Path.

examples.text: Давай, счастливого пути и хорошей дороги!
examples.trans: Go ahead, safe travels and have a good road!

examples.text: Ты сам выбрал этот страшный путь.
examples.trans: You chose this terrible path yourself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.trans: I don't know.
As you all know...

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верное').

examples.trans: Well, probably somewhere in the archive.
He has probably already come home.

examples.text: Наверное, что-то серьёзное у вас. Девочка уже две недели лежит в областной клинике!
examples.trans: It must be something serious for you. The girl has been lying in the regional clinic for two weeks already!

хозяйка.gloss: landlady, hostess, mistress of the house

meanings.en: landlady, hostess, mistress of the house
meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'landlady, hostess, mistress of the house' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Right, hand over the money, landlady.

examples.text: Хозяйка квартиры живёт на первом этаже.
examples.trans: The landlady of the flat lives on the ground floor.
My wicked landlady kicked me out.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are hiding', paired with 'спрятаться'.

examples.text: Да никуда я не пряталась! Я контролировала ситуацию.
examples.trans: I wasn't hiding anywhere! I was controlling the situation.
I wasn't hiding anywhere!

examples.text: Ты должна спрятаться в очень надёжном месте.
examples.trans: You must hide in a very reliable place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'what for, why', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What have you come for?
What's that for?
Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, come on, Dad!
Well?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.
Do you like gum?

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'when', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.
Oh yeah? When?

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'man, real man, bloke' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You should have acted like a real man!
He's a decent bloke.

examples.text: Что мы, мы? Тебе надо было как мужик!
examples.trans: What do you mean, we? You should have acted like a man!

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'дить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to drive (a car); to lead'.

examples.trans: You're driving.
She drives a car very well.

examples.text: Если тебе плевать на дочь, то мне нет! Ты водишь.
examples.trans: If you don't care about our daughter, I do! You're driving.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Has something happened?
Somehow I'm tired.
I can't see it somehow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to happen', paired with 'случаться'.

examples.trans: What happened?
Nothing will happen.

examples.text: Марина, я вам обещаю: со стеной ничего не случится.
examples.trans: Marina, I promise you: nothing will happen to the wall.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.
There, look.
You'll see!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'between, among', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You two sort it out between yourselves here.
There are no secrets between us.

examples.text: Ну ладно, вы тут между собой договоритесь.
examples.trans: All right, you two sort it out between yourselves here.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other').

examples.trans: For your information, I am the chairman of the court.
Books, notebooks, and so on.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, здесь же ребёнок, мы завтракаем. А телевизор, между прочим, наш!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, there's a child here, we're having breakfast. And the television, by the way, is ours!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I was only looking.
Just one.
I was only looking!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'renovation, repair' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The flat has been nicely renovated.
The car is being repaired.

examples.text: Три комнаты, кухня, ремонт. Какая квартира была!
examples.trans: Three rooms, a kitchen, renovated. What a flat it was!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
I'll do it tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'year' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I've been working here for four years.

examples.text: Это было давно, тридцать лет назад.
examples.trans: That was long ago, thirty years back.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'ago; back, backwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!
Five minutes ago.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago! I signed the order myself!
